title: Python Engineering Mastery
subtitle: From your first line of code to a production Python service
description:
A single path from absolute beginner to production-ready Python engineer.

You will not read your way through this. Every lesson ends in code you write and
run, every concept is assessed against real execution, and the final assessment
is a business requirement document rather than a multiple-choice test.

The path deliberately front-loads the ideas that everything else depends on —
the execution model, names and objects, functions — then broadens into
collections, error handling, objects, files, HTTP, testing and unattended
automation. It closes with four projects whose scaffolding fades until you are
handed nothing but requirements.
outcomes: Write, run and debug Python programs with confidence
Choose the right data structure and justify the choice
Design functions and classes that other people can read and test
Handle failure deliberately, so problems are visible rather than silent
Read and write files, JSON and CSV without losing data
Consume HTTP APIs resiliently: timeouts, retries, pagination, auth
Write test suites that catch real defects and survive refactoring
Build automation that runs unattended and can be diagnosed from its logs
Take a business requirement and deliver a designed, tested, deployable service

modules.title: Foundations: How Python Thinks
modules.summary: The execution model, names and objects, decisions and repetition. Everything else in the curriculum assumes this module.

lessons.title: What Python Is, and What Happens When You Run It
lessons.summary: Programs, interpreters, bytecode and the REPL — the mental model everything else rests on.

lessons.title: Variables, Types and the Label Model
lessons.summary: Names are labels attached to objects, not boxes holding values — and that one idea explains a whole category of bugs.

lessons.title: Making Decisions: if, elif, else
lessons.summary: Branching, truthiness, and writing conditions that a reader can verify at a glance.

lessons.title: Repetition: for, while, and Loops That Terminate
lessons.summary: Iterating over data, counting with range(), and the discipline that stops a while loop running for ever.

modules.title: Data Structures and Algorithms: Choosing, and Justifying
modules.summary: Tuples, sets, comprehensions, sorting, complexity and the queue and heap types in the standard library — the vocabulary for picking a container and defending the pick.

lessons.title: Tuples and Unpacking: Data With a Fixed Shape
lessons.summary: A tuple says 'this many things, in this order, and it will not change' — and unpacking is how you read one without index arithmetic.

lessons.title: Sets: Membership, Deduplication and Set Algebra
lessons.summary: When the question is 'is it in there?' or 'what is in both?', a set turns a loop into an operator and O(n) into O(1).

lessons.title: Comprehensions: Describing a Collection Instead of Building One
lessons.summary: A comprehension states what the result *is*, rather than the steps that accumulate it — and stops being a good idea at exactly the point it stops fitting on one line.

lessons.title: Sorting: Key Functions, Stability and Custom Order
lessons.summary: You almost never write a comparison. You write a function that says what to compare — and stability lets you build compound orders out of simple ones.

lessons.title: Complexity: Choosing a Structure You Can Defend
lessons.summary: Big-O is not about speed. It is about what happens when the input gets ten times bigger — and it is the vocabulary for justifying a data structure in review.

lessons.title: Stacks, Queues and Heaps From the Standard Library
lessons.summary: Three access patterns — last-in-first-out, first-in-first-out, and smallest-first — each with a container that makes it O(1) instead of O(n).

modules.title: Core Python: Functions, Collections and Failure
modules.summary: Naming behaviour, choosing data structures deliberately, and handling errors so that failures are visible rather than silent.

lessons.title: Functions: Naming a Piece of Behaviour
lessons.summary: Parameters, arguments, return values, scope, and the mutable-default trap that catches everyone once.

lessons.title: Lists: Ordered, Mutable, Everywhere
lessons.summary: Indexing, slicing, the mutation methods, and the copy semantics that decide whether your change is visible somewhere else.

lessons.title: Dictionaries: Lookup by Meaning
lessons.summary: Key–value mapping, the .get() idiom, counting patterns, and why dict lookup is O(1).

lessons.title: Errors and Exceptions: Failing Well
lessons.summary: try/except/else/finally, choosing what to catch, raising deliberately, and why silent failure is worse than a crash.

modules.title: Professional Python: Objects, Data, Services and Operations
modules.summary: Everything between 'my code works' and 'my code runs in production': classes, files and formats, HTTP clients, tests, and automation that survives being unattended.

lessons.title: Classes: Bundling State With Behaviour
lessons.summary: __init__, methods, properties, inheritance, dunder methods — and when a function would have been better.

lessons.title: Files, Paths and Data Formats
lessons.summary: Context managers, pathlib, JSON and CSV — reading and writing without losing data or leaking handles.

lessons.title: APIs and HTTP: Talking to Other Systems
lessons.summary: Requests, status codes, authentication, timeouts, retries and pagination — the difference between a demo client and one you can run unattended.

lessons.title: Testing: Proving It Works, and Keeping It Working
lessons.summary: pytest, arrange-act-assert, fixtures, parametrisation, mocking — and writing tests that survive a refactor.

lessons.title: Automation: Code That Runs Without You
lessons.summary: Idempotency, structured logging, CLI design and failure handling for jobs that run at 2am with nobody watching.
